items.text: Changed: **Freeze** now hears everything that sounded last: the grid's own sounds, recorded and sampled sounds (not drum banks, which have no pitch), and the field's sounds. Pressing Play no longer adds a stray note to what it remembers.

in the **hold hand**, press and hold an empty cell for about a third of a second and Freeze holds the last notes for as long as you keep pressing. A quick tap on an empty cell still does nothing. This works in full screen, with no pads.
Fixed: the Freeze pad's symbol vanished while it was on (yellow on yellow). It now shows dark on the yellow, like the other bar buttons.

a **Tuning** choice next to Scale and Root note (in the heads-up display and in the Field pane, kept in step). *Equal 12* is the ordinary tuning and changes nothing. *Just 12* tunes the twelve notes to clean whole-number ratios, so chords ring pure. *Equal 8* and *Just 8* use eight notes to the octave; each scale note moves to the nearest of them, so some fall between piano keys. It is kept with your look and with a saved piece. A scale that already sits between keys (Just) is left as it is.
**Freeze** (the fermata pad, key F). It takes the last few different notes you heard and holds them as a drone made of the field's sound. Tap to lock it on, tap again to let go; or hold and let go.
**Swell** (the hairpin pad, key S). While you hold it the sound and the room rise, and both ease back when you let go.
Changed: the small bar that floats beside whatever you tap in the G-code editor is now called the **G-code remote** (the Remote for short). Screen readers announce it by that name.

Changed: the **line-ups menu** (hold the play button) is two columns of related pairs instead of one long column, about half the height: Reading and Shuffle, Tide and Shoreline, Cross and Four winds, Scatter and Two tides, Ripple and Drain (out and in), Grow and Shrink, Radar and Whirl, Orbit and Breath. Rows are a little tighter.

Fixed: the clean-screen spectrum bars now sit exactly under the grid's own columns, including the uneven ones a beat pattern makes (Primes, for one). They follow the grid when the pattern, the direction or the window changes.

Changed: in the clean screen the spectrum bars now **play all the time**, faint along the bottom, moving with the music. Hold outside the grid and they all rise to the maximum together; when they reach the line the controls come back. Let go early and they sink back to the music.

Changed: the clean-screen bars are now a **live frequency spectrum** of what is playing (low notes at the left, high at the right, one bar for each grid column). As you hold they rise toward the line where the grid begins and settle there together; the music keeps moving them on the way. With nothing playing they sway gently instead.
